closingKeywordReason: Human-answered fork: Refs, not Closes; the issue is flagged for manual reconciliation of its upstream half (prefer-first-party-mcp.js stays with PR #1618).
assumptions: Raw copy from the harness 14.0.0 dist instead of `harness hooks init`: init without --force skips locally modified files and with --force would clobber the canary forks of sentinel-pre/sentinel-post/telemetry-reporter; it would also touch prefer-first-party-mcp.js wiring. No per-file refresh command exists (`harness hooks add` adds wiring, not a refresh).

adoption-tracker, block-no-verify, pre-compact-state, protect-config synced byte-identical to 14.0.0; read-hook-stdin.js added. Each canary-local change in those four (skill-events.jsonl path, protect-config fail-closed on missing file_path) is already present upstream.

sentinel-pre, sentinel-post and telemetry-reporter carry deliberate canary changes upstream does not have (deny-by-default Bash gating during taint, symlink/sibling-safe workspace check, NotebookEdit coverage, untrusted-source scoping; honest telemetry send guarded by scripts/check_hook_customizations.mjs). A raw sync would regress them, so the canary copies were kept and only upstream's readHookStdin seam was ported in, with upstream's per-hook policy (sentinel-pre fails closed on a failed read; sentinel-post and telemetry-reporter stay fail-open).
Every 14.0.0 upstream copy of the 7 hooks already uses readHookStdin, so there is no upstream readFileSync(0) remainder and no upstream issue text to draft for this bug.

The 5 canary-owned call sites read stdin through a synchronous EAGAIN-retrying readSync loop (readStdinToEof) instead of async process.stdin iteration, because every seam is a synchronous `readStdin(): string`; going async would change GuardianDeps/DiffResolutionDeps and validate.mjs main() signatures. No deadline, matching blocking-read semantics (a slow `gh pr diff` producer must not be cut off).
Each call site keeps its existing policy for a genuinely unreadable stdin (briefing/guardian return '', main-deps prompt falls back to defaults, validate.mjs reports a usage error).

scripts/highest-stable-tag.mjs did not reproduce on main (it never touches process.stdin, so its pipe stays blocking); it was converted anyway for consistency and its late-payload test is a guard, not a reproducer.

The reader exists in three copies: ts/src/util/read-stdin.ts, agents/skills/lib/read-stdin.mjs (skills lib is vendored into consumer repos and takes no dependency on ts/, the is-main.mjs precedent), and inline in scripts/highest-stable-tag.mjs (the script is staged standalone by release-advance-latest.test.ts, so a lib import broke it). They are imported modules, not roots, so they are not added to entropy/performance entryPoints (the entropy ratchet reports no finding on them).

ts/test/canary-cli-coverage2.test.ts no longer calls the real defaultMainDeps().prompt: with read-to-EOF it waits on the vitest worker's never-closing stdin (the full suite hung there). It only ever returned because the non-blocking read threw EAGAIN. Same deliberate exclusion main-deps-defaults.test.ts and guardian-cli-default-deps.test.ts already document.

ts/test/briefing-cli.test.ts 'reads a diff from stdin via --diff -' also only passed because the read threw EAGAIN on the runner's never-closing stdin. MainDeps gains an optional readStdin seam (same pattern as genDataSelfCheck) that briefing's diffDeps prefers over readStdinToEof, and the test injects empty stdin. guardian/cli.ts already has its own readStdin seam, so it needed only the one-line swap.

On a TTY the company-knowledge wizard's prompt now reads to EOF like any blocking read (it reads all piped lines once by design and never printed its prompt text); that pre-existing wizard design is out of scope.

The ts CLI seams are pinned by a unit test of the helper, a real-process late-payload test of the helper under O_NONBLOCK stdin, and a static guard that no fd-0 readFileSync remains in hooks/ts/src/scripts/skills lib (prefer-first-party-mcp.js allowlisted pending #1618).
